title: Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov
summary: IBM's Deep Blue defeated reigning world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a six-game match completed on 11 May 1997, winning 3.5 to 2.5 under standard tournament time controls.
significance: A documented computer-chess milestone: IBM records the result as the first time a reigning world chess champion lost a match to a computer opponent in tournament play.

geography.note: IBM first-party material identifies the 11 May 1997 rematch venue as the Equitable Center in New York City.

verification.note: IBM's 1997 Annual Report dates the match victory to 11 May 1997 and records the first-in-tournament-play claim; IBM first-party retrospective material independently records the 11 May 1997 Equitable Center rematch and 3.5–2.5 result; IBM Research describes Deep Blue as the chess machine that defeated the reigning World Chess Champion in a six-game match in 1997.

sources.title: IBM Power6 presentation — Deep Blue retrospective
